s: Traditional public forum (streets, sidewalks, parks "time out of mind"):
content-neutral rules get the time, place and manner test.
Designated public forum (property the government intentionally opens for expressive activity): the same as a traditional forum while it remains open.

Limited public forum (opened for particular subjects or speakers, such as student activity funds or school facilities after hours): restrictions must be reasonable in light of the forum's purpose and viewpoint neutral (Rosenberger; Good News Club, 2001).

Nonpublic forum (government property not open for expression, such as airport terminals in ISKCON v. Lee, 1992, and polling places in Minnesota Voters Alliance v. Mansky, 2018): restrictions must be reasonable and viewpoint neutral.
